as_read: Mixed: one sponsor-funded crossover with a named primary outcome favors a standardized extract at 200 mg/day in stressed healthy adults; other small oral trials differ in population and name no primary outcome in the abstract; 4 g was null versus placebo in fatty liver disease and 6 g impaired memory speed acutely.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: trait anxiety on the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory after 4 weeks
studies_to_add.quote: After four weeks of rosemary extract intake, significant improvements were found in trait anxiety scores measured using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory and heart rate variability, as indicated by a decreased low-frequency/high-frequency ratio.

stop_list: Marker-standardized extract (rosmarinic acid 5 mg, diterpenes 8 mg per 200 mg) can't be compared with labels printing extract mass only.
35318738's abstract does not say the 4 g is per day.
clinician_items: 21877951: the 6,000 mg single dose significantly impaired speed of memory (P<.01), with other deleterious cognitive effects that were less consistent, in adults with mean age 75.
stored_rating_note: Stored applicability text says extracts were not studied; 41312013 and 37758539 studied extracts. Stored outcome is a single-dose effect with benefit at the lowest dose and harm at the highest, and the abstract names no primary outcome. Stored positive_weak is not out of line with the read, but mixed fits better.
